sentences.text:
Lakshmi Mistanna Bhander & Ors vs The State Of West Bengal
on 6 July, 2017
 1
06/07/2017
Ardr Crr 2463 of 2014 Lakshmi Mistanna Bhander & ors.
Vs. The State of West Bengal Mr. Pratip Kumar Chatterjee, ...for the petitioners.
Affidavit of service is taken on record.

Challenging the judgment dated 30/4/2014 passed by the learned Chief Judge, City Sessions Court, Calcutta, in connection with Criminal Appeal no. 95 of 2013, the present accused petitioner has filed this application.
According to him, the learned trial Court as well as the learned first Appellate Court could not appreciate the evidence in its proper perspectives.
He added that the seizure witnesses have not been examined and that the report of the Public Analyst has not been exhibited properly.
It appears from the order of the learned trial Court that he has recorded evidence, and after a threadbare discussion, has passed the order of conviction against the present petitioner.
Challenging the said finding, the present petitioner has approached before the first Appellate Court.

After discussing all other issues, learned Appellate Court has come to a finding that the learned trial Court ought to have followed the provisions of Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for passing appropriate sentence.
According to the present petitioner, the said "Lakshmi Mistanna Bhander" is a proprietorship firm and Section 17 relates to only for corporate house.
Be that as it may, actually there is no such finding done by the learned Sessions Judge.
In such circumstances, it would be appropriate to direct the learned trial Court, in view of the direction given by the learned first Appellate Court, to pass an order afresh.
The present petitioner will be at liberty to take all the defence that is available to him at the time of hearing before the learned trial Court.
With this direction, the CRR stands disposed of.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, be given to the parties.

(Siddhartha Chattopadhyay, J. )
